extracted.intended_audience: playwrights, comedians, literary scholars, students and theorists of humor
extracted.subtask_description: Theory-driven guidance for creating and analysing comic (comédie) characters and scenes — focusing on what makes a character or situation laughable, how to observe and generalize comic traits, and how to stage them for corrective/social effect.

rubrics_metrics.name: Unconsciousness / inattention to self
rubrics_metrics.description: “Il y a un aspect de sa personne qu'il ignore… c’est par là seulement qu'il nous fera rire.”
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A comic character must display an element of self-ignorance — a side of themselves they do not perceive. Laughter springs from noticing a trait that is visible to others but escapes the character’s self-awareness. Examples: M. Jourdain’s contradictions, Vadius preaching against verse-reading then pulling out verses. Anti-pattern: a character who is aware and self-mocking is less laughable in this register.

rubrics_metrics.name: Mechanical rigidity / automatism (raideur, automatisme)
rubrics_metrics.description: “Raideur, automatisme, distraction, insociabilité, tout cela se pénètre, et c'est de tout cela qu'est fait le comique de caractère.”
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Comic effect often derives from behavior that functions like a machine — fixed habits, stiff/formulaic reactions, repetition, and 'solidification into character'. Portray repeated, mechanical responses (self-repetition) so the behaviour reads as a mechanism. Anti-pattern: too much psychological depth or variability undermines the impression of a mechanical type.

rubrics_metrics.name: Generality / typification (the character as type)
rubrics_metrics.description: “Peindre des caractères, c’est-à-dire des types généraux, voilà donc l'objet de la haute comédie… Tout personnage comique est un type.”
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Comedy aims at the general: create characters who function as types (frames) that many people can recognise and fit into. Use abstraction and selection of characteristic traits so the figure stands for a class. Technique: show several exemplars or variants of the same type to emphasize generality (the naturalist method). Scoring note: the more convincingly the character functions as a repeatable type, the stronger the comic effect.

rubrics_metrics.name: Frameability / repeatability of the trait
rubrics_metrics.description: “La condition essentielle… est que la particularité observée apparaisse tout de suite comme une espèce de cadre, où beaucoup de personnes pourront s’insérer.”
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Choose traits that can be perceived as a 'cadre' — explicit, recognisable features that many people might share. This allows the audience to generalize and laugh at the class, not only the individual. Practical advice: favor traits that map neatly onto social roles or recurrent behaviors.

rubrics_metrics.name: Professional / role-based comic (comique professionnel)
rubrics_metrics.description: “Toute profession spéciale donne… certaines habitudes d'esprit et certaines particularités de caractère… Nous l’appellerons… le comique professionnel.”
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Professions and social functions furnish ready-made frames: trade habits, jargon, ceremonial attitude and self-importance. Use these professional mannerisms to build types (e.g., doctors in Molière). Warning: exaggerating an isolated profession beyond social context can make the figure less comic (it risks becoming implausible).

rubrics_metrics.name: External / inductive observation (method of comedy)
rubrics_metrics.description: “Tout autre est le genre d'observation d'où naît la comédie. C’est une observation extérieure… la méthode et l’objet sont… de même nature ici que dans les sciences d’induction.”
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Create comedy by observing outward signs and aggregating them into generalities, rather than probing inner psychological depths. The comic writer should collect analogous surface features across persons and abstract the quintessence. Anti-pattern: attempting to dramatize deep interior motives defeats the comic abstraction that makes types laughable.

rubrics_metrics.name: Balance of depth and superficiality
rubrics_metrics.description: “Il la faudra profonde, pour fournir à la comédie un aliment durable, superficielle cependant, pour rester dans le ton de la comédie, invisible à celui qui la possède…”
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A successful comic disposition should be durable (deep enough to recur) but remain superficial in experience so that the subject does not perceive it. Aim for traits with staying power but that manifest at the surface; this balance maintains comic stability and the necessary invisibility to the subject.

rubrics_metrics.name: Corrective / social function of laughter
rubrics_metrics.description: “Le rire accomplit sans cesse un travail… rappeler à la pleine conscience d'eux-mêmes les amours-propres distraits et d'obtenir ainsi la plus grande sociabilité possible des caractères.”
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Comedy is not merely entertainment; laughter has a mild corrective role — to expose and correct socially harmful vanities or rigidities. When designing comic effects, consider the social corrective impulse: make the flaw recognizable and amenable to correction. Scoring note: comedy whose laugh can plausibly prompt self-correction scores as socially effective according to Bergson.

rubrics_metrics.name: Immediate correctability (practical usefulness of the laugh)
rubrics_metrics.description: “corrigible immédiatement, pour qu'il n'ait pas été inutile d’en rire,”
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prefer faults that can be remedied on the spot or through social sanction; laughter should have a practical, re-adaptive outcome. If the trait is incurable or destructive, the comic effect loses its social utility and may become merely cruel.

rubrics_metrics.name: Vanity as the central risible defect
rubrics_metrics.description: “Ce mélange est la vanité… le défaut essentiellement risible est la vanité.”
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Vanity is a primary, fertile source of comic material: self-admiration based on imagined regard of others. Use scenes where characters display disproportionate self-regard or pretend grandeur (e.g., a small man trying to seem big). Many other comic defects orbit vanity; targeting it often yields reliable comic returns.

rubrics_metrics.name: Contradiction between speech and action (hypocrisy)
rubrics_metrics.description: “Il n'est pas rare qu'un personnage comique blâme une certaine conduite en termes généraux et en donne tout aussitôt l'exemple…”
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Expose characters whose words and deeds contradict each other: moralising speech followed by immediate counterexample. Such contradictions reveal unconsciousness and provoke laughter. Practical device: set up a didactic line and immediately show behavior that undermines it.

rubrics_metrics.name: Tone: indulgence toward subject but socially embarrassing
rubrics_metrics.description: “pleine d’indulgence pour elle-même afin qu'elle s’étale sans scrupule, gênante pour les autres afin qu'ils la répriment sans pitié,”
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Portray the comic character with a tone that is indulgent (so the character acts without self-censure) while the situation is socially awkward enough to invite reproach. The audience should both pity/indulge and see the need for social correction. Avoid mean-spirited cruelty that lacks corrective intent.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of names/titles and labels to signal type
rubrics_metrics.description: “Le Misanthrope, l'Avare, le Joueur, le Distrait… voilà des noms de genres… Le titre même des grandes comédies est déjà significatif.”
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Titles and labels compress a character into a recognizable type and prime the audience to generalize. Using an evocative name or label can make a character’s type instantly intelligible and broaden the comic resonance (it helps a character to become a common noun in the language).

rubrics_metrics.name: Populate with simplified secondary exemplars
rubrics_metrics.description: “Un instinct remarquable porte le poète comique… à en faire graviter d’autres tout autour qui présentent les mêmes traits généraux.”
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Surround the central comic figure with secondary characters who are simplified copies or variants of the same type: this multiplicity confirms the generality and multiplies the comic effect. Technique: create a small social cluster whose members instantiate the type’s main trait in different ways.

rubrics_metrics.name: Combinability and versatility of the comic trait
rubrics_metrics.description: “capable enfin… de s’additionner à tous les vices et même à quelques vertus.”
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Choose traits that can combine with other faults or even some virtues so the comic effect can reappear in many guises. Versatile traits make the comic source renewable across situations and characters; design for recombination to sustain long-term comic interest.
